questions.question: Describe a shoe box, a tin and a ball by the shapes of their faces and the number of flat and curved surfaces, and compare the tin with the ball.
questions.expected_answer: Shoe box: 6 rectangular faces in matching pairs, 6 flat surfaces, 0 curved. Tin: 2 circular faces and 1 curved surface. Ball: no faces, 0 flat surfaces, 1 curved surface. The tin and the ball both have a curved surface, but the tin also has two flat circular faces while the ball has none.

questions.question: Sort a cube, a sphere, a cylinder and a square pyramid into flat surfaces only, curved only and both, giving the reason for each.
questions.expected_answer: Flat only: cube, because all 6 faces are flat squares, and square pyramid, because its square and 4 triangles are all flat. Curved only: sphere, because it has no flat faces. Both: cylinder, because it has 2 flat circular ends and a curved side.

questions.question: Explain how to build a square pyramid from cut-out polygons and how building it checks the description of its faces.
questions.expected_answer: Cut 1 square and 4 equal triangles whose bases match the square's sides. Tape a triangle to each side of the square, fold them up and tape the slanted edges together at the apex. If 3 triangles were used there would be a gap and with 5 one would have nowhere to go, so building confirms that a square pyramid has exactly 1 square face and 4 triangular faces.
